basis: Who reads it: F3 members are mostly men in their 30s to 50s (local reports put the typical man in his early 40s, with a range from late 20s to 70), professionals with families. So every style uses bigger type (18px body, 13px+ labels instead of 10-12px) and the build checks contrast (WCAG AA, 4.5:1) for every text colour.

How they read it: mostly on phones, and early (workouts start before dawn, in "the gloom"). So there are dark options for 5am scrolling and light options for daytime, and the phone layout is checked for each.
Where: The Fort is Fort Mill / the Carolinas. Two styles lean on that: Carolina blue, and brick and stone for "The Fort".

What is popular in 2026: earth tones (olive and terracotta especially), one saturated accent on a calm neutral base, large expressive headings, and accessibility-first colour. The six cover each of those.

What you have liked so far: dark, condensed capitals, quieter rather than rounded-everything, and no fixed accent colour. So only two of the six are rounded, and the six use six different accent hues.
Limits: there is no official F3 Nation colour palette to follow, and no survey of members; the audience notes come from local news coverage of F3 groups.

styles.name: Gloom
styles.summary: Pre-dawn indigo with a faint sunrise glow, a periwinkle accent and dawn-peach highlights; soft floating cards.
styles.why: Named for F3’s own word for the pre-dawn workout. A calm dark for reading at 5am that is softer than the current near-black, with an accent nobody else in local fitness uses.

styles.name: Carolina
styles.summary: Clean daylight white with Carolina blue, navy ink and brick-red highlights; big plain type and hairline rules.
styles.why: Local pride, and the most readable of the six: dark text on white at large sizes, the safest choice for men in their 40s and 50s reading in daylight.

styles.name: Brick & stone
styles.summary: Limestone paper, brick-red accent and charcoal ink; serif headings, italic labels, matted flyers, square corners.
styles.why: Takes "The Fort" literally, with a heritage men’s-club feel like the editorial run-club brands. Grown-up and warm, and it reads like a newsletter.

styles.name: Trailhead
styles.summary: Dark olive with a terracotta accent and pale-olive highlights; dashed notebook rules and lower-case labels.
styles.why: The 2026 earth-tone trend (olive and terracotta) applied to an outdoor group that works out in parking lots and parks in all weather. Earthy without being beige.

styles.name: Volt
styles.summary: Graphite with an electric lime accent; keeps the bold condensed capitals and square corners.
styles.why: The closest to what you have now, re-coloured: the sporty, high-energy look of current training brands, one saturated accent on a dark neutral. Best for pulling in younger guys.

styles.name: Fellowship
styles.summary: Bright white and pale aqua with a deep teal accent and coral highlights; round cards and a floating pill header.
styles.why: The friendliest first impression, for the FNG who finds the site before his first post: open, modern, welcoming, and calm rather than hardcore.
